newsitem.title: ITALY: Finmeccanica chairman says will quit.
newsitem.headline: Finmeccanica chairman says will quit.

text.p: The chairman of Italy's state-controlled engineering group Finmeccanica, Fabiano Fabiani, said on Friday that he would resign after the group's parent company ordered a radical shake-up.
A company statement said Fabiani "intends to submit his resignation as chairman of Finmeccanica at a shareholders' meeting already called for April 30". It gave no other details.

The move followed a statement from Finmeccanica's parent company, state holding IRI, on Thursday on a restructuring of operations which business analysts took as a condemnation of the present management.
IRI, bidding to speed up Finmeccanica's much delayed privatisation and open the way for strategic alliances, said it would create a single operating unit to run the firm's industrial concerns.
Finmeccanica itself will become the group's financial holding.

"The new organisation will make necessary alliances easier, at the same time safeguarding shareholders' interests," IRI said, adding that the restructuring would also make the privatisation process more rapid.

Finmeccanica, which is one of Italy's biggest industrial concerns, with aerospace, defence, transport and energy interests, made a loss of 540.4 billion lire ($318 million) in 1996 after an extraordinary writedown of 575 billion lire.
Finmeccanica said last year it hoped to be privatised in 1997, but that is now seen as impossible and no further sell-off timetable has been given.
IRI called for the creation of a swift new industrial plan at the company to take advantage of the changes.
"There is a need to intensify efforts to improve rapidly profitability and efficiency, as well as its competitive position in various business areas," IRI added.

Finmeccanica said last month it made the extraordinary writedown to cover future restructuring and investment plans for its defence and aeronautical divisions and to proceed more decisively with a policy of alliances.

Earlier this year, the Italian group signed a memorandum of understanding with Britain's General Electric Co Plc (GEC) to study opportunities for co-operation between their respective defence sector companies.
Analysts said the talks might lead to a partnership of huge potential that could speed up the consolidation of Europe's splintered defence industry.

Finmeccanica has predicted that it will return to the black in 1997. Turnover totalled 13.88 trillion lire last year from a previous 12.84 trillion, with orders at the end of December standing at 28.22 trillion lire.
The Italian group accounts for 70 percent of the domestic defence business.

Its defence interests include aerospace and satellite division Alenia and helicopter maker Agusta. Through Alenia it is involved in numerous European aircraft projects, including a regional aircraft joint venture and Eurofighter.
